transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-10-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Eric Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (AstraBio CTO), Samir Khan (Head of MLOps), Priya Desai (Security), Connor Li (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick POC scoping focused on cost modeling and unit economics for AstraBio's lab-assistant product. Discussed workload sizing, per-token assumptions, batching/caching knobs, and pilot timeline. Action: Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet; customer to share workload samples; schedule benchmarks.
Topics: success criteria, throughput & latency targets, token estimates, batching/caching impact, hosted vs dedicated pricing, quantization options, compliance notes.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Eric is our SE who will run the bench stuff. Quick round-robin?
[00:10] Lena: Hi all, Lena here, CTO at AstraBio. We're building a lab assistant for internal researchers and later a clinical-facing assistant. Cost is a big gating factor.
[00:20] Samir: Samir — MLOps. We'll own the pilot infra and benchmarks.
[00:25] Priya: Priya from security — interested in compliance and KMS/HSM stuff.
[00:30] Eric: Great. High level — goal today: nail down success criteria for a 4-week POC, get a rough token budget, and align on benchmark approach.

[02:15] Maya: Can you describe expected usage? QPS, avg tokens per request, synchronous vs async?
[02:30] Samir: Short answer: start small. We expect 5 internal heavy users during pilot, 1000 queries/day roughly, but if successful ramp to 100k queries/day in production. Prompts vary — many are structured lab notes, so prompts average 120 tokens, completions about 300 tokens — so ~420 tokens per call.
[03:05] Connor: Also we do some large summarization jobs (1k+ input tokens), but those are infrequent — maybe 5% of requests.

[05:00] Eric: Ok let's ballpark. Pilot: 1k queries/day * 420 tokens = 420k tokens/day ~12.6M tokens/month. Production ramp (100k q/day) => 42M tokens/day -> ~1.26B tokens/month.
[05:20] Maya: For cost assumptions we typically show hosted per-token and an effective dedicated per-token estimate for reserved capacity. For example, hosted inference on model X: ~$0.03 per 1k tokens (that is $0.00003 per token) as a baseline. Dedicated reserved capacity can net you ~40-60% lower effective token cost depending on utilization and batching.
[05:55] Samir: That per-token number seems low/high? (slight overlap) Can you show a worked example?
[06:10] Maya: Sure — pilot: 12.6M tokens/month at hosted price $0.03/1k = 12.6M/1000 * $0.03 = $378. Production at 1.26B tokens -> 1,260,000 * $0.03 = $37,800 / month. With dedicated at 50% discount effective cost ~ $18.9k.
[06:35] Priya: Are those numbers including context-window overhead? We have long contexts for some jobs so tokenization overhead matters.
[06:50] Eric: Good call — we model prompt+completion and repeated prefix tokens separately. If you can leverage prefix/KV caching for repeated context (like patient protocol templates), effective billable tokens can drop 10-30% depending on reuse. For summarization, caching not applicable.

[08:15] Lena: We need P95 latency <350ms primarily for researcher interactive flows. For large batches it's ok to be slower. Also need budget constraint: initial monthly spend <$5k for pilot.
[08:40] Maya: Pilot under $5k is doable — we can size it. If we assume hosted billing and run limited load and aggressive caching we should stay under that. We'll show a couple of scenarios in the spreadsheet: conservative (no caching), realistic (some prefix caching), and optimized (batching + caching + quantized model on dedicated).

[10:00] Samir: On batching — we expect some natural batching for batch jobs. For interactive flows, batching is trickier. What's the throughput/latency trade-off?
[10:15] Eric: Continuous batching in our runtime groups concurrent requests; it improves GPU utilization and lowers per-token unit cost, but can add a queuing delay. For your interactive target P95<350ms, we can allow batch windows up to ~20ms and still hit the target for many models. For high concurrency you get better batching, so cost per token drops. We'll include a chart: concurrency vs effective cost.
[11:00] Connor: What about quantization — can you run int8 or int4 for these models to reduce instance size?
[11:15] Eric: Yes, we support int8 and int4 profiles; int4 reduces memory and may allow cheaper GPU families, but there's sometimes a small accuracy delta. For assistant-style tasks we'd test int8 first. For private deployments you can pick the quant profile during rollout. We'll log quality/regression metrics.

[13:20] Priya: Security question: what about KMS integration and logs? We need customer-managed keys and audit logs for every request.
[13:35] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and audit log shipping. We'll share SOC2 docs and the KMS integration guide. For pilot we can run hosted but with network isolation options or dedicated with private networking depending on your risk appetite.

[15:10] Eric: Back to unit economics — let me show a couple of quick hypotheticals in the call: scenario A (hosted, no caching) — 1.26B tokens/month -> $37.8k/mo as said. Scenario B (hosted + prefix caching 20% reduction) -> $30.24k/mo. Scenario C (dedicated reserved, 50% effective discount + caching 20%) -> ~$12.1k/mo. These are elastic examples; final contract would reflect reserved capacity pricing, egress, and retention.
[15:50] Samir: Good — can we run an actual benchmark so we trust these numbers?
[16:05] Eric: Yes — we propose a 24-72 hour benchmark: 1) representative sample of 1k prompts you send; 2) run at scaled concurrency to simulate 100k q/day footprint but capped for pilot; 3) measure P95 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, and billable token counts. We'll run both hosted and dedicated Node prototype.
[16:40] Maya: We'll need your sample prompts and any PII redaction rules. Also define success criteria: e.g., P95 latency <350ms for interactive set, throughput target X qps for batch set, cost per monthly active researcher <$50.

[18:00] Lena: Success criteria: 1) P95 <350ms for interactive; 2) accuracy/quality on 50 eval prompts (we'll share eval set) meets baseline; 3) pilot cost < $5k; and 4) security checklist signed off.
[18:20] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll translate those to pass/fail thresholds in the benchmark plan.

[20:05] Connor: One more nuance — some requests include retrieval from our internal vector DB and we only want the model call for the final composition. How do you advise counting tokens there?
[20:25] Eric: Typical pattern: do retrieval server-side, send distilled context + prompt to LLM. If you include long doc snippets repeatedly, use prefix caching or compress the context. Billed tokens are whatever you send to the model plus completion. So reducing context size and caching repeated prefixes drives down cost. We'll show sample tokenization.

[22:40] Samir: For the benchmark harness — can you support replaying requests with original timing to emulate spikes?
[22:55] Eric: Yes, our test harness supports time-series replay, ramp-up, and constant QPS. We'll run a few profiles: steady-state, 10x spike, and a heavy summarization bucket.

[25:10] Priya: For compliance, small question — do logs contain full prompt text by default? We need ability to mask PII and control retention.
[25:25] Maya: You can configure logging policies; default hosted logs store prompts for 30 days for debugging but we can turn off or redact fields. For Private, you control retention. We'll include that in the security doc pack.

[28:00] Eric: Operational knobs we'll test: batch window configuration, KV/prefix cache TTLs, quantization profile, and autoscaling thresholds. Each affects cost + latency differently; we'll produce a sensitivity table in the model.

[31:30] Maya: Quick worked example in the spreadsheet we'll send: Pilot (14 days): 12.6M tokens expected -> hosted cost ~ $378 as we said, but we add a margin for benchmarking traffic and repeat runs so pilot budget request $1.5-2k. That keeps you under the $5k ask.
[32:05] Lena: Ok good. For production math we need per-active-user cost. If an active researcher averages 50 calls/week -> 200 calls/month -> at 420 tokens/call = 84k tokens/month per user. At $0.03/1k that's ~$2.52/user/month (hosted). That seems reasonable.
[32:40] Maya: Right — and with dedicated + caching you could be <$1/user/mo. We'll show both.

[35:00] Samir: What about initialization overhead if we warm KV caches? Does that add cost?
[35:10] Eric: Warming doesn't add billable tokens unless you actually call the model. You can prefetch embeddings into local cache without model calls sometimes. For prefix caching, first-time requests use full tokens, later reuse saves tokens. We'll show warm-up plan.

[38:20] Connor: Timeline: we want pilot kickoff next week if possible.
[38:30] Maya: Proposed timeline: Oct 16 — Redwood sends spreadsheet & bench plan; Oct 19 — AstraBio shares samples; Oct 22 — benchmark runs; Oct 23 — review; Oct 27 — pilot kickoff (2-4 weeks). We can be flexible.

[40:50] Priya: Security deliverables due before production are SOC2 summary, KMS guide, network architecture diagram.
[41:05] Maya: We'll attach those to the follow-up email.

[44:10] Samir: A couple of risk items: 1) model regressions with quantized runs, 2) utilization variance for dedicated pricing — if utilization low, effective cost rises.
[44:30] Eric: We'll include sensitivity: utilization at 30/50/80% and show the per-token effective numbers. Also a QA plan to run eval prompts against each quant profile.

[47:00] Lena: If benchmarks look good, what's the procurement step?
[47:10] Maya: We'll provide a draft SOW and pricing options: short-term pilot (month), then 3-12 month reserved capacity for dedicated with SLA. Legal/procurement will likely request standard terms; we'll engage our sales ops.

[50:05] Maya: Recap & next steps: 1) Redwood send cost-model spreadsheet + bench plan (Maya/Eric) by 10/16; 2) AstraBio share 1k sample prompts + eval set by 10/19 (Samir); 3) Run hosted + dedicated benchmark 10/22; 4) Review 10/23 and decide pilot kickoff.
[50:35] Connor: Sounds good.
[50:50] Priya: Ok thanks, will review security docs as they come.
[51:05] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench slots and attach the spreadsheet.
[51:20] Lena: Appreciate the clarity. Speak soon.
